answers.q1: Cargo (Rust, toolchain >=1.96, pinned in CI as 1.96.0). There is no separate install step. Cargo fetches dependencies during the build, so run: cargo build --workspace. To fetch dependencies only, run: cargo fetch.
answers.q2: cargo test --workspace --features unstable-index (CI first runs this, then runs cargo test --workspace --features pcre2). The AGENTS.md shortcut `cargo test --workspace` also works, but it skips the index tests.
answers.q3: cargo test --test integration regression:: (tests/regression.rs is a module of the `integration` test target, which is tests/tests.rs per Cargo.toml [[test]]. The `regression::` filter selects only that module.)
answers.q4: cargo fmt --all --check (this is the CI rustfmt job). The CI docs job also runs: RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items --workspace. CI does not run clippy.
answers.q5: Cargo.lock and fuzz/Cargo.lock (lockfiles, per AGENTS.md). Also the man page and shell completions, which are produced by ripgrep's build process (build.rs) into target/ build output. Do not hand-edit target/ either. No vendored directories were found.

q1.reason: Identifies Cargo, says no separate install step, and gives cargo build --workspace and cargo fetch, consistent with the accepted answer.

q2.reason: Includes cargo test --workspace and the pcre2 run, but the primary command adds an unstable-index feature not in the truth and claims the plain workspace command skips tests.

q3.reason: cargo test --test integration regression:: exactly matches an accepted command.

q4.reason: Gives cargo fmt --all --check, adds the cargo doc command, and correctly says CI does not run clippy.

q5.reason: Names Cargo.lock and target/ as non-hand-edited and says no vendored directories, matching the truth; the build.rs outputs lie in target/ and don't contradict it.
